title: Arnold Johnson: ensemble only and the Hamilton, Ontario dance
summary: Asked about choruses on Arnold Johnson records, he says he played only ensembles and tells of the Hamilton dance.

story.theme_name: Drink, drugs and the bandstand's casualties
story.community_name: Drugs and drink on the bandstand and the road

blocks.x: I wanted to ask you one thing before I forget it. Did you take any choruses with Arnold Johnson on the records?

No, never. Just ensemble. Just ensemble. Well he was a piano leader and he featured himself. And the only time I would get a good crack at it was when he would leave the bandstand like in Hamilton, Ontario. He'd go off with the committee and have drinks or something. Then the first trumpet player would double on piano. And I'd take over. I'd leave the band. I'd play pop tunes. The tunes of the band were like down home in Tennessee and all that kind of stuff. Because they didn't know any addiction to it. But I always found a spot where I could live a little bit, you know. I remember we had to go back on the bandstand that night. We got off the bandstand without playing God Save the Queen. And we were off the bandstand packing up. And they come back there and I was like, Mr. Johnson you didn't play God Save the Queen. Well Johnson says, why? He says, well that's the way they close the dances in Hamilton, Ontario. You play God Save the Queen. So we go back on the ball and as we leave in they give us each an imperial quart of whiskey. We went and we got on that train loaded around with booze or something. Imperial quarts, you know those big quarts. I love that little, it was one night, other fellas were sleeping but I got up and I said, I'm going to eat my breakfast in this hotel. It's the last thing. It was the Royal Connaught. It was strictly English. And Hamilton, have you been there?
